dossier.architecture: Minimal-roller deployed pickup and shooter with mechanically linked amp bar; redundant climbers.

subsystems.intake: Four-roller over-bumper collector kept light for rapid retract.
subsystems.transfer: Indexer stores the note and doubles as the amp delivery path.
subsystems.scoring: Independent top/bottom launcher, asymmetric wheel count and virtual-four-bar amp guide.
subsystems.endgame: Two motors per climber; team reports continuing to climb with one entire climber removed.
subsystems.controls: Source-loading fallback, heading presets, shot lock/reacquire and tested autonomous routines.

versions: One climber removed for repairs at Bonney Lake; redundant side preserved endgame. Core design intentionally limits additional actuators.
dossier.analysis: A useful reliability case: redundancy protects an actual scoring function, and source loading remains possible after intake loss. Assess the mass/electrical cost against the specific failure it survives.
limits: Intermediate undocumented changes are not inferred; specifications and plans retain their source context.

context_documents.title: 2024-1778 · Minimal intake rollers and redundant climb capacity have different justifications
context_documents.body:
# 2024-1778: Minimal intake rollers and redundant climb capacity have different justifications

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The over-bumper collector uses four rollers after early prototyping. An indexer retains the note and serves amp delivery through a virtual linkage. The top/bottom launcher uses asymmetric wheel contact. Each climber has two motors, and the team describes continuing after one side was removed following a failure.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team ties the reduced collector to sufficient pickup performance with lower mass, and the unusual climb power to single-side operation and imperfect chain alignment. Asymmetric contact is reported to improve spin/stability and range.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Simplicity should be evaluated per task rather than imposed uniformly. Removing an unnecessary roller can improve collector dynamics, while adding climb reserve can preserve a match outcome after damage. Those are compatible engineering decisions. Single-side climbing also changes structural loads and roll, so redundancy is only real if the frame and scoring mechanisms tolerate the alternate load case.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test the minimum collector with worn notes and wall contact. Validate disabled-side climb loading and harmony clearance, rather than extrapolating from two-side nominal lifts.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: 1778 CAD/Code Release
facts: Two lower rollers helped bend the note during acquisition and guide the Amp shot; one lower roller had sent it above the bar. Team reported 0.2-inch intake compression and 0.5-inch shooter compression without horizontal squeeze. The virtual four-bar eliminated a separate Amp-bar motor.
source_reviews.limitations: Team recollection; CAD was linked and uninspected.

source_reviews.title: Chill Out 2024 Robot Code
source_reviews.locator: master: Controls.kt; IntakeWrist.kt, ShooterRollers.kt, ShooterWrist.kt, Climbers.kt, ClimberHook.kt; CenterNoteCommand, ShooterShootCommand, ShooterAmpShootCommand and climb commands
source_reviews.review_basis: Read Kotlin source from team-published master archive.
facts: Pickup runs collector and shooter feed together, then raises the intake while centering. Two digital line breaks distinguish storage and further travel. Amp uses driver approval in Amp wrist state. The two hooks each have a NEO master and follower.
source_reviews.limitations: Public release is a code snapshot. Physical dimensions, specific event deploys and climb recovery history require separate evidence.

source_reviews.title: Chill Out robot archive
facts: Connects the robot name with the district and Championship season and identifies a separate pit interview and robot CAD.
source_reviews.limitations: Interview captions were unavailable on retry; archive text gives no additional mechanical dimensions.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Zappy Feet combines a deployable roller collector with a wristed scorer that handles acquisition, storage, and release. A shaped Amp path follows the shooter wrist through a virtual four-bar, allowing a second scoring geometry without allocating a motor to its deployment. The mechanical coupling works with a control sequence that distinguishes collecting, centering, aiming, and firing. Two independent hook sides share the chassis with these mechanisms but get their own motor pairs. The code shows where software coordinates the collector with the climbers and where the operator still decides to release a note.
source_review.piece_flow: In the floor routine the intake is commanded down, then its rollers run alongside the shooter intake command. After acquisition the collector rises in parallel with centering. The lower line break indicates storage. The centering command pulls briefly, then feeds outward slowly while the upper beam is occupied and stops when it clears. Source loading uses a different wrist pose but reuses the shooter and centering routines. Speaker shots use flywheel spin-up plus authorization. Amp delivery uses the feed rollers after operator approval and the Amp wrist state.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The collector wrist has its own motor but reads an absolute sensor through the roller controller. The shooter wrist uses its master motor relative encoder and has a follower; the linkage makes bar geometry follow wrist geometry. The climb extension command explicitly demands Intake Down. That establishes a software dependency between the two motions. Whether its purpose was clearance, deployment order, or another constraint needs a geometry review.

subsystems.name: Collector and acquisition
subsystems.construction: Separately powered roller and wrist functions; absolute intake angle from the roller controller. Team reported 0.2-inch compression.
subsystems.operation: The floor routine waits for its angle command before starting parallel acquisition. Source loading skips the floor collector.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team published compression. The code describes the sequence but gives no prototype rationale for individual roller positions.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Driving the collector and destination together allows an early handoff, provided the leading edge reaches the downstream nip before it loses the upstream contact.
subsystems.interfaces: Collector wrist position gates roller operation through the command sequence, and the shooter acquisition command is the deadline for parallel collection.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: A loose absolute sensor connection can remove angle feedback even when the wrist motor remains functional. Inspect the sensor through full collector travel.
subsystems.unknowns: Roller number, tread, and entry envelope await physical or interview review.

subsystems.name: Shooter, staging and Amp bar
subsystems.construction: Team describes two lower rollers, one top roller and a virtual four-bar. Software separates two regulated flywheel motors, a feed motor, two line breaks and a wrist.
subsystems.operation: Speaker tracking checks wrist alignment, tag availability, chassis heading and flywheel readiness before timed feeding, with separate preset branches. Amp uses the feed roller and coupled bar.
subsystems.team_rationale: The extra lower roller fixed an Amp shot above the bar and improved intake. Linkage addressed concern about notes falling into the bellypan without requiring another motor.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Wrist-angle error affects both launch and Amp alignment. The shown speed check uses top wheel feedback despite both motor velocities being available, so test asymmetric wheel recovery.
subsystems.interfaces: Upper beam clearance terminates centering; the lower beam represents storage. The linkage maps wrist angle to bar location without a separate actuator state.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check both beam transitions with worn notes. In the centering command a continuously blocked upper beam can keep slow feeding active until interrupted.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact linkage pivots, wheel diameters, and shot dispersion.

subsystems.name: Climbers and drive coordination
subsystems.construction: Two oppositely signed hook objects each use one master and one following NEO with brake mode and current limits.
subsystems.operation: Extend starts both sides and stops them individually as calculated extension passes 0.7; retraction similarly stops each side near zero.
subsystems.team_rationale: The reviewed code demonstrates independent control, while the claimed single-side field recovery remains unverified here.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Independent stopping handles position mismatch; equal encoder readings cannot establish equal chain load or confirmed engagement.
subsystems.interfaces: Master encoder and configured drum circumference/reduction establish the travel estimate. The extend command also owns the intake wrist.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Verify encoder zero and paired-motor direction after service. Validate asymmetric loading separately from nominal dual-side operation.
subsystems.unknowns: Actual hook, cable and drum construction, attachment load, and trap capability.

revisions: The team reports adding the second lower roller after the single-lower-roller Amp prototype failed. The virtual bar entered after an early archetype and remained close to the sketched geometry.
transferable_principles: Tie a passive scoring guide to a powered joint only after checking its pose across the full travel.
A positive sensor transition gives a stronger staging reference than fixed run time alone.
disconfirming_conditions: If worn notes bridge the upper beam indefinitely, centering needs a different stop condition.
If wrist or linkage play consumes Amp clearance, sharing the axis can cost more than a dedicated guide.
remaining_gaps: Interview-dependent collector details and any single-side climb incident remain open; public CAD was not inspected.
